key_insight: Foundation ML interatomic potentials can capture simple scalar and some bond-length ordering in correlated perovskite oxides, but they still fail on purely local spin-state transitions and fully symmetry-resolved vector order.
engineering_relevance: This work shows where off-the-shelf MLIPs are reliable for atomistic simulation in complex oxides and where DFT or domain-specific training remains necessary for predictive modeling.
method: Ran 1 ns molecular dynamics on 80- and 160-atom supercells.
Swept temperature from 50 to 300 K for LaMnO3, LaCoO3, and NdNiO3.
Compared three foundation MLIPs against low-temperature ordering behavior with no system-specific training.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on three isostructural perovskites revealed a hierarchy: NdNiO3 scalar order was captured, LaMnO3 bond-direction order was captured in magnitude but not symmetry, and LaCoO3 spin crossover was not captured.
watch_item: Off-the-shelf foundation potentials may miss on-site multiplet physics and symmetry-specific ordering, so they should not be assumed reliable for strongly correlated spin-state transitions.
paper_title: Bond, orbital and spin order in d4/d6/d7 perovskite oxides: successes and limitations of foundation interatomic potentials
